title: Scoped obstruction: selected PR1094 has no improving single whole-helper relocation
head: 489f9011862dcd53a7785e151d3af0a1cd08250a
body:
The selected PR1094 packing has **no legal, strictly improving single whole-helper relocation** between existing bins when widths, call times and actual source-event windows stay fixed. This adds a complete exact census, proof and opt-in replay in `research/frontier1094-single-relocation/`. No new kappa, supplier adoption or global optimum is claimed.

## Result and scope

- All **336,456,862 capacity-feasible distinct-bin role/destination pairs** are counted through 20 integer rank classes, covering 69,120 roles and 32,256 bins.
- Exactly **19** pairs would lower the idle moment; **all 19 fall outside their strict destination windows**. The certificate records their identities, event positions and window endpoints.
- The sign is uniform for every real `0<a<1`: moving width `w` changes free ranks `(x,y)` to `(x+w,y-w)`, and strict concavity gives an improvement iff `x+w>y`. No floating-point score or root-ordering assumption is used.
- A real positive fixture creates a legal worsening move and detects its improving inverse `39+9 -> 48+0`; the retained owner audit accepts both altered maps. These are in-memory controls, not new physical constructions.

Geometry, helper widths and baseline admission explicitly reuse Josie Elliston's pinned PR1091 audit, including eleven owner mutation controls. The relocation enumeration and exponent-uniform proof are new; a separately implemented geometry audit is not claimed. Local calls, bit supplier and inherited extra charges are fixed. Swaps, neutral paths, multi-role repacking, new schedules/words and idle-axis transfers are excluded.
